As many of you might remember, Voat recently had an ad for Mythos Christos.

I'm not a heavy reader, so take my review with a grain of salt, but I really enjoyed reading it. The plot and actual action was enough to keep you reading, though there's only so much room for "excitement" in a realistic archaeological caper. But the story maintained enough small twists and intrigued to keep it interesting throughout. Some portions of the conversation seemed a bit condescending. The initial college discussion leaned towards a "definitely real" /r/atheism self post despite very solid research, but if you tough through that, it's smooth sailing.

The strongest points, in my mind, were the intertwining of factual historical data with the story. In the Afterword, the author clearly explains where artistic license was used, but I found many of the clues for the dig to be grounded in reality. The use of Gematria and Greek mathematical philosophies showed the author's devotion to his work. Without spoiling anything, I can safely say that the mathematical interpretation of the "fish and bread" miracle was one of my favorite parts to learn about.

If you have don't already have a half-read book in your hands and need something to fill the time, I highly recommend Mythos Christos. It did the trick for me as a casual reader, but I think it'll also intrigue some of the more serious ones.
